text:
anya: quick copy review — found two spots where "unsaved changes" copy is inconsistent: the editor toast says `Unsaved changes` and the close-modal prompt says `You have unsaved changes. Discard?` Link to screenshot: https://files.redwood/snap.png sam: looks good to call this out. my instinct: make the toast a short status, and the modal explicit with actions. propose: toast = `You have unsaved changes` (non-interrupting) modal title = `Unsaved changes` body = `You have unsaved changes. Save before closing?` actions = `Save` (primary), `Discard changes` (destructive), `Cancel` (secondary/neutral). marta: +1 to being explicit in modal. language nit: `Discard changes` reads clearer than just `Discard`. also prefer `Keep editing` over `Cancel` — more descriptive for screen readers and users who skim. des: want to flag button order and visual treatment. destructive action should be visually distinct (red) and on the left if we follow some platform patterns, but our existing pattern in the console usually has primary on the right. suggest we keep primary (Save) on the right, destructive (Discard changes) on the left and red, and `Keep editing` as a ghost button. Also check keyboard order for accessibility (tab order matches visual). :warning: liam: small accessibility notes: - toast should be in an `aria-live="polite"` region so screen readers hear it but it's not disruptive. - modal should set focus to modal title and announce the body. - buttons should have `aria-describedby` to link to the modal body if labels are terse. anya: good calls. can we also agree on exact microcopy for both contexts so I can update Figma and the copy file? draft: - toast (short): `You have unsaved changes` - toast (with action): `You have unsaved changes — Save now` (action label `Save`) - modal title: `Unsaved changes` - modal body: `You have unsaved changes. Save your changes or discard them.` - buttons: `Save` (primary), `Discard changes` (destructive), `Keep editing` (secondary) marta: tiny nit: `Save your changes or discard them.` feels a hair formal. maybe `Save your changes or discard them — changes will be lost.` but that's wordy. alternative: `Save your changes or discard them. This cannot be undone.` maybe too alarmist. i lean to: `Save your changes or discard them. Unsaved changes will be lost.` des: prefer the shorter: `Save your changes or discard them. Unsaved changes will be lost.` includes the consequence. sam: +1. also consider the case where autosave exists. do we need a conditional body: if autosave is on -> `Changes are saved automatically` with different buttons? anya: yes, autosave flag will change copy. for autosave ON: toast -> `All changes saved` (green) modal -> `All changes are saved` and only show `Close` button. i'll add that branch in variant notes. liam: snippet for toast modal ARIA to include in the code notes: ```
You have unsaved changes

Unsaved changes

You have unsaved changes. Unsaved changes will be lost.
``` anya: awesome. @design-bot can you link the current button patterns doc so I can match token styles? :pray: design-bot: Pinned doc -> https://docs.redwood/design/button-patterns. Primary = right, destructive = left (red), secondary ghost = neutral. marta: can we do a quick a11y pass once this lands? I can run the modal with NVDA/VoiceOver and check the announcement order. des: i'll take keyboard + visual tests. anya: thanks all — i'll update the figma and post the new copy in the #design-copy folder. planning to ship this with the next editor patch. :rocket
